claims.claim_en: The word 'نِحْلَةً' is used metaphorically (istiarah) to mean a gift or mahr (an act of giving).
claims.rhetorical_effect: Frames the dowry/mahr as a gracious gift; softens legal term into emotive giving.

claims.claim_ar: توكيد بالازدواج: الاقتران المتوازي لكلمتين متقابلتين/متقاربتين في المعنى (مثل: «هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا») لتأكيد الصفة.
claims.claim_en: Emphatic duplication (takrar): the pairing of two near-synonymous adverbs (as in 'هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا') functions to intensify/confirm the pleasantness, analogous to the construction 'وَنُدْخِلُهُمْ ظِلًّا ظَلِيلًا'.
claims.needs_review_reason: Inference based on a parallel example in the commentary (ظِلًّا ظَلِيلًا); the provided chunks do not comment explicitly on هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا in this ayah.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Intensifies positive appraisal of consuming what is given; stylistic emphasis and pleasant-sounding closure.

claims.claim_ar: إيجاز/اختزال: نصب كلمة «نِحْلَةً» على المصدر بمعنى الإيتاء كاختصار عن ألفاظ أطول، وهو أسلوب مُقدَّر ومُقَدَّم في التفسير.
claims.claim_en: Conciseness (ijaaz): the use of 'نِحْلَةً' in the accusative on the masdar (verbal-noun) to mean 'giving' represents a compressed expression instead of a longer formulation; the commentary notes this construction and calls the passage stylistically good.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source discusses a grammatical/stylistic point ('انتصابها على المصدر' and praises the phrasing); interpretation as rhetorical concision is plausible but mingles grammar and rhetoric.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Creates brevity and elegancy in legal/ethical instruction, making the command concise and forceful.
